risks.note: Staffing and workforce management is sensitive to economic cycles, business sentiment and hiring trends; slowdowns in manufacturing, retail, IT services, BFSI, logistics or global trade can directly reduce workforce deployment and hiring demand. Mitigated by a diversified portfolio across sectors, workforce categories and geographies and by an asset-light, technology-enabled operating structure.

The business operates in a highly regulated environment spanning labour laws, wage regulations, social security compliance, taxation and immigration policies across multiple jurisdictions; regulatory change can alter operating models and raise compliance costs. The Company also flags potential non-compliance risk on the new Labour Codes, including incorporating revised requirements into payroll systems and increased financial exposure from changed wage structures and social security obligations - while treating the Codes as a net opportunity versus unorganised players.
risks.risk: Regulatory and compliance risk (labour laws, wages, social security, immigration)

risks.note: Growth depends on attracting, deploying, engaging and retaining workforce across blue-collar, grey-collar, professional and gig categories; higher attrition and competition for skilled talent can impair operational efficiency and service delivery. Attrition is structurally high - permanent worker turnover was 115.2% in FY 2025-26 and permanent employee turnover 50.8%, both above the prior year.

As a technology-driven staffing organisation operating proprietary platforms handling large volumes of associate, candidate and client data, the Company is exposed to ransomware, system intrusions and data breaches; a compromise could disrupt operations, expose sensitive data and cause financial, reputational, regulatory and legal consequences. Mitigations include a Cyber Security Council led by the CTO and Business IT Heads, ISO-aligned practices, periodic VAPT, DLP, 2FA, WAF, MDM and endpoint security, and a centralised network/firewall/log-monitoring architecture across offices.

The staffing industry is highly competitive with increasing pricing pressure, evolving service expectations and technology-led disruption; loss of key clients or sustained pricing pressure can hit profitability and market positioning. Countered through integrated workforce solutions, a diversified client base, long-standing relationships and higher-value offerings such as GCC staffing, managed services and AI-enabled workforce solutions.
risks.risk: Client concentration and competitive intensity / pricing pressure

risks.note: International staffing operations are exposed to geopolitical developments, local regulatory change, visa restrictions, currency fluctuations and region-specific labour market risks across APAC and Middle Eastern markets. Mitigated by geographic diversification, continuous evaluation of country-specific regulatory environments, local operational expertise and flexible deployment strategies.

As the digital ecosystem expands, sustained adoption and engagement across associates, gig workers and enterprise clients is critical for platform scalability and monetisation; the Company relies on platforms such as Hamara HR, Hamara Jobs and TaskMo for workforce engagement and scalable service delivery.

Managing a workforce base of significant scale across geographies, sectors and client locations carries risks around deployment efficiency, service quality, productivity and execution consistency; addressed with technology-led workforce management systems, AI-enabled automation, standardised operating procedures and real-time monitoring.
